text:
maria: Quick sync — we need a concise apples-to-apples spec for kernel selection + batching perf tests. I keep seeing ambiguous baselines (auto-kernel vs tuned) and mixed synthetic/replay setups. Can we lock definitions for TTFT, TPOT, p95/p99, and goodput vs QPS here?
ben: +1. Short defs from my side: TTFT = time from request arrival to first token emitted. TPOT = total processing overhead time (includes server-side queueing + compute for full sample). Goodput = completed useful tokens/sec (excludes retries/backpressure). QPS = raw request/sec hitting ingress. They diverge when batching/KV cache is used. :eyes: 
kai: For the harness, we should explicitly separate two axes: traffic shape (replay vs synthetic) and kernel selection policy (fixed per-run vs auto). Example run commands I use: 
```
# synthetic: gaussian prompt lengths
loadgen --mode=synthetic --dist=gaussian --mean_len=64 --std=10 --rps=200 
# replay: replay recorded client traces, preserving arrival times
replay-run --trace=prod_20260222.json --preserve-timing --parallel=8
```
We must log config with kernel_hint and batching params.
sam: Important question — do we warm up KV cache in both baseline and comparison runs? If warmup is only for tuned kernels we bias results. I propose: 1) cold-start series (no KV warm) 2) warmed series (10k tokens of warmup matching distribution) 3) steady-state long-run.
yara: For apples-to-apples, also pin the model weights and quantization level. Kernel selection must be explicitly stated: either `kernel=auto` or `kernel=jit-fused` or `kernel=math-optimized`. A/B requires same quantization.
ben: Agree. Also metric math: report p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and TPOT, and report goodput at each latency SLO (e.g., goodput@p95<120ms). Use CDFs for visibility.
perf-bot: automated-run: run_id=20260222-42, config=(replay, kernel=auto, batching=max32/t=6ms), results: goodput=312 tokens/s, QPS=52 req/s, TTFT_p50=38ms, TTFT_p95=112ms, TTFT_p99=210ms, TPOT_p95=128ms.
maria: Nice. But can we define a pass/fail rule for regressions? I think: relative change >5% in goodput or absolute increase in TTFT_p95 >20ms -> fail on presubmit. For release canary: >2% goodput drop or any p99 spike >50ms alert.
kai: For reproducibility, include this minimal JSON artifact with every run: 
```
{
  run_id: "...",
  mode: "replay|synthetic",
  kernel_policy: "auto|fixed:jit-fused",
  batch_max: 32,
  batch_timeout_ms: 6,
  kv_warm_tokens: 10000,
  seed: 12345
}
```
(we don't need strict JSON quoting here in the log blob, but the CI artifact should be valid JSON)
sam: On the synthetic vs replay equivalence: we should compute a "workload distance" metric (KL on prompt length + KL on token-per-request distribution + arrival-IPI divergence). If distance < threshold, we can use synthetic for perf runs; otherwise use replay traces.
yara: One more practical note: measure queue time separately (time in scheduler queue before batch formation) and include batch-size distribution histograms. That explains why goodput can be > QPS * avg_tokens when batching groups requests into larger multi-token batches.
maria: Action items: (1) formalize the pass/fail thresholds in the perf playbook, (2) add the minimal run artifact to CI, (3) add KV warm/cold labels to all historic traces, (4) add workload-distance check to the harness. I'll file the playbook PR after this thread. :thumbsup:
ben: I'll draft the p95/p99 visualization template (CDF + latency heatmap + batch-size breakdown).
kai: I'll add the run flags and ensure `replay-run` emits the run artifact.
sam: I'll produce a short script to compute workload distance and KV-warm labeling.
perf-bot: queued: create-ticket "perf-playbook-202602" assigned to @maria.
